title: Sucic opens, and Inter score three in half an hour
description: Petar Sucic's first Inter goal won him man of the match, Djed Spence came on for his debut, and Club Brugge visit San Siro on Tuesday.
mast_alt: Nerazzurri Daily Edition No. 40, Sunday, October 11, 2026 — Sucic opens, and Inter score three in half an hour

blocks.html: Inter beat Parma 3–0 at San Siro on Saturday, with all three goals inside the first 31 minutes. Petar Sucic, the midfielder, scored his first Inter goal and was named man of the match; Hakan Çalhanoğlu, the penalty taker, and Marcus Thuram, the forward, got the others. Inter have 16 points from six matches, and Club Brugge come to San Siro on Tuesday.

blocks.h3: Sucic's first Inter goal, and the man-of-the-match award
paras: Edoardo Corvi, the Parma goalkeeper, played a weak pass out of his area in the 13th minute. Sucic took the ball off Mandela Keita, the Parma midfielder, and finished with his left foot. It was his first goal for the club.
Sucic said afterward: “sono contento per il premio” — he was pleased with the award, and said what mattered was winning in front of Inter's own fans.

blocks.h3: Spence comes on for his debut as Chivu rotates
paras: Djed Spence, the defender, came on for Andy Diouf, the midfielder, in the 73rd minute, for his first Inter appearance. He had been out for about two months. In the 83rd minute he crossed for Lautaro Martínez, the captain, whose header went just over the bar.
Cristian Chivu, Inter's head coach, said: “abbiamo fatto riposare chi ha dato tanto in nazionale” — the players who gave a lot for their countries were rested.

blocks.h3: Club Brugge come to San Siro with Inter on no points
paras: Inter host Club Brugge on Tuesday, October 13 at 3:00 PM ET, 21:00 CEST, in matchday 2 of the Champions League league phase. It is their first home match in the competition, and they arrive 25th of 36 with no points after losing 2–1 at Real Madrid.
Chivu's press conference is Monday at 8:30 AM ET, 14:30 CEST, at Appiano Gentile, Inter's training ground.

blocks.h3: Corriere dello Sport: the referee missed the penalty, and VAR fixed it
paras: Corriere dello Sport's refereeing review says Kevin Bonacina, the referee, missed Diego Carlos, the Parma defender, stepping on the right foot of Francesco Pio Esposito, the Inter forward. The penalty was given after an on-field review. The paper calls that and a missing booking for Sucic in the 14th minute “le uniche sviste” — the only lapses.
blocks.kicker: CORRIERE DELLO SPORT VIA FCINTER1908 · OCT 11

blocks.h3: Club Brugge arrive top of their league, with Sommer in goal
paras: FCInterNews reports that Club Brugge won 4–1 away at RAAL La Louvière, a seventh win in eight league matches that keeps them top in Belgium. Their goalkeeper is Yann Sommer, Inter's for two seasons. FCInter1908 quoted him on Sunday: “Ho vissuto momenti memorabili con l'Inter e ora con il Brugge” — memorable moments with Inter, and now with Brugge.
It was Inter's second Serie A clean sheet of the season. Thuram was born in Parma and has scored against them in five straight meetings.
